clinician.trajectory_summary: 26-year-old female presented with 3 weeks of activity-related right tibial pain localized to the anterior and medial mid-leg, with mild swelling but no erythema, trauma, or systemic symptoms. Initial X-ray demonstrated a well-defined intramedullary sclerotic lesion of the mid-tibial shaft with narrow zone of transition and no fracture line (E001). Subsequent CT imaging confirmed sclerotic lesion with medullary canal obliteration and specifically excluded aggressive features including sinus, sequestrum, periosteal reaction, soft tissue component, cortical nidus, or old fracture line (E002, E006). Based on these characteristic imaging findings and exclusion of alternative diagnoses, the patient was diagnosed with intramedullary osteosclerosis and managed conservatively with NSAIDs and activity modification according to pain tolerance (E004).
